‹#›
To consider 
When describing noses, you can use the adjectives hooked, pointy, flat, button. 
Lips are describe as thin or thick. Also, full. 
Eyebrows can also be described as thick, thin or bushy. 
If you want to describe a piece of clothes, you need to follow the regular pattern of adjectives. The correct verb to use when talking about it is -wear- E.G. She is wearing a beautiful single red, silk, European nightgown. On top of it, she has a gorgeous, golden silk shawl.

-Lauren: Hey, Liam. How are you?
-Liam: Doing great. How about you?
-Lauren: Great as well. Wow you look good.
-Liam: Oh thanks. I bought this single blue, rayon, German shirt on my trip.
-Lauren: It is beautiful and it does match your big, round, blue eyes. 
-Liam: So my mum told me, ha, ha, ha,. Hey, are you planning to go to Tyler’s party?
-Lauren: Ummm. I want to but...I don’t know him quite well and he seems to be not very friendly.
-Liam: No way, he is super friendly and quite fun. 
-Lauren: Really? The tall, thin, muscular guy with prince-charming hair who is so popular?
-Liam: That one! Do not worry, I’ll pick you up and you’ll be my date. 
-Lauren: Great, then. Wear something nice. 
-Liam: I always do.

texts: When we describe people, we can talk about their appearance and personality.

She is a tall, thin woman with light complexion. She has shoulder-length, blond, straight hair and big, round, blue eyes. Also, she has a pointy nose and full red lips. She is wearing a plain white, cotton blouse. Finally, we can say she is not an easy person.
